title: Siegard telemetry report
description: How a stretch of work with this framework happened — not what it delivered. Written by `bin/telemetry.py` at `<telemetry_root>/<stamp>.json`, where the stamp is the UTC moment the window closed, and read by `/siegard-telemetry` to write the prose report beside it. Every figure here is counted from something on disk: the delivery roots' captured runs, the plan nodes' notes, the specification's decision log, the repository's history, and the harness's own session transcripts under its projects directory — the one source outside the project, and the only one that records which agents ran and what each cost. Nothing here is estimated, and nothing is recalled: a section whose source could not be read carries its reason in `provenance` and its data absent, never a plausible value. The report exists so the framework's maintainer can rule on a friction report without another conversation — so it names the framework version it measured, the effort every agent and skill was configured at, and the window it covers, and it is refused over a window whose stamp already has a report, the way a run is refused under a name that exists.

contract_version.description: Which contract this report was written against. siegard-telemetry/1 carried no `usage` on a session's own entry in `harness.sessions` — `agent_totals` was the whole of what a report counted. siegard-telemetry/2 counted only the agents a session spawned directly: an agent spawned by another agent had a transcript on disk and no row here, so `agent_totals` under /2 is a floor over any window where a skill ran inside a spawned context, and is not comparable to a /3 total over the same window. An earlier report is still the count it was when it was written, read by tolerant readers, and never rewritten to match. siegard-telemetry/4 adds `outcome` to every decision the window added and `outcomes` beside them — whether the field a decision filled still reads as its landing commit wrote it, and by which route it was changed where it does not — and attributes each session's own usage to the skill it was running, under `harness.sessions[].by_skill` and `harness.skill_totals`. A /3 report carries neither and is read as it was.

project_root.description: The directory `siegard.json` sits in, resolved — the anchor every relative path in this report is spelled from.

since_resolved_from.description: Where the opening bound came from: `named` when the invocation stated it, or the path of the previous report whose `until` this window continues from. A window is never inferred from memory of when a session began.

window.description: The stretch of wall-clock time this report covers, both bounds UTC. Everything below is filtered to it: a transcript entry, a run step, a commit or a decision outside it is not in this report.

version.description: The installed framework's version, read from its plugin manifest. Null where the manifest is absent or names none — and a report over a framework that cannot say which version it is measures a framework nobody can resolve to what ran.

contracts.description: Every `contract_version` constant the installed schemas declare, keyed by schema file — so a figure here can be read against the exact contract the artifacts it counts were written under.

transcript_roots.description: Every transcript directory a session in this report was read from: the project's own first, then any sibling directory — one named for a subdirectory of the project the harness was opened in — that held a session whose recorded working directory sits under the project. A sibling that merely shares the name's prefix, such as a neighbouring project, is never read.

transcript_root.description: The directory the harness keeps this project's session transcripts in — its projects directory, one subdirectory per working directory the harness was opened in, named by that directory's path with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9] replaced by a hyphen. Read, never written; an internal format of the harness and not of this framework, which is why every read of it is held to a probe first and every failure to read it is a stated reason rather than an absent number.

skill_totals.description: `by_skill` summed across every session in the window: the session side of the cost, by the skill the session was running. Beside `agent_totals`, which is the agent side by type, these are the two halves of what a stretch of work spent — and this is the half a report reading `agent_totals` alone leaves out.

human_turns_in_window.description: When a person typed, inside the window — the timestamps of every turn that was a human's message rather than a tool's result. What was typed is not here: a telemetry report counts, it does not quote a conversation. A user-role entry the harness wrote — a background task's completion notice, a local command's echo, a reminder it injects — is not a person typing and is not counted; a paste a person made is.

by_skill.description: This session's own turns and tokens by the skill it was running, keyed by the skill's bare name — `none` before the first Skill call. A Skill call names the span from itself to the next; the person's own turns inside that span count toward it, so every figure here is a ceiling per skill and is read as one.

usage.description: The tokens this session's own turns spent inside the window — never a subagent's, which `agent_totals` already carries. A report reading `agent_totals` alone sees roughly half of what a task with several delegations actually cost: the orchestrating turns between them are the other half, and this is where they are counted.

sessions.description: Every session transcript that holds at least one entry inside the window.

spawn_depth.description: How many spawns separate this agent from the session: 1 where the session spawned it, 2 where an agent the session spawned did, and so on. An agent's `usage` is its own turns alone at every depth — a parent's row does not carry its children's, the way a session's `usage` does not carry its agents' — so the rows at every depth sum without overlap.

parent_agent_id.description: The `agent_id` of the agent whose transcript holds this spawn, or null where the session's does. What a row's parent was is what tells a reader which context invoked a skill: a fork that spawned this framework's agents is a parent row here, and its own cost is the orchestrating turns between them.

agent_type.description: The subagent type the skill spawned, as the harness recorded it — a shipped agent's name where a skill delegated to one, or a harness built-in.

usage.description: Token usage summed over every assistant message in the agent's own transcript. Null where the transcript was not found — then `unavailable` says so.

repeats_earlier.description: True where an earlier invocation in this window spawned the same agent type under the same description. It is the mechanical half of the rework question: a repeat is a candidate for rework, and whether it was one is the reader's to judge from the two transcripts.

agents.description: Every subagent the harness spawned inside the window, at every depth, in the order it was spawned — the session's own spawns, read from its transcript, and each agent's spawns, read from that agent's transcript once it was found. An agent whose transcript was not found hides whatever it spawned, and its `unavailable` says so.

scripts.description: Which of this framework's scripts the command line invoked, by file name.

exit_code.description: The exit status where the harness recorded one. The harness marks a non-zero exit at the head of the tool's result and marks nothing for zero, so a null here with `exit_marker` false is a command that exited zero or whose result was never recorded — the two are told apart by `unavailable`.

problems.description: The count a validator's `N problem(s)` line reported, where the result carried one.

commands.description: Every shell command inside the window that invoked one of this framework's scripts, with what it exited and what its validator counted.

runs.description: Every captured run under every delivery root whose first step started inside the window, read from the record `run.py` wrote.

baseline.description: What the current log was compared against to find what the window added: the commit that last touched it before `since`, or the reason no such baseline exists — in which case every current entry is listed and the reader knows why.

items.description: One decision the log gained inside the window, as the log states it, plus `outcome`: `landed` (the commit and instant the entry first appears in the log's history), `state` (stands, revised, node-gone, unreadable, unlocated), `value_now`, `revised_by` (every later commit that changed the located field, each with its subject and its route) and `days_to_first_revision`. The comparison is the field as the landing commit wrote it against the field at the window's close — the working tree, or the last commit at or before `until` where later commits exist — never the log's own `decided` text, which paraphrases.

outcomes.description: The tally beside `added`: how many decisions stand as their landing commit wrote them, how many were revised and by which route the first revision came, with the meaning of every state and route beside the counts. Never a share: what a reader acts on is the list of the revised ones in `added[].outcome.revised_by`, each with its commit — and the one distinction that matters, that only `corrective` and `hand-edit` are a person disagreeing while `framework` is the framework revising itself.

text.description: The note verbatim — a classified `## Notes` entry as its opening spells it, or an epic's `uncovered` entry whole.

notes.description: Every classified note standing in a plan under the work root, at the moment of the report — not filtered to the window, because a standing note is the state the window's work ran under.

scope.description: The denominator. Cost is only readable per unit of work: how many tasks each initiative maps, how many carry an implementation record now, and which records landed in this window.

provenance.description: One entry per section above: where it was read from, or why it could not be. A report is complete when no entry carries a reason; the prose report's closing verdict is computed from this list and from nothing else.

configured.description: How one shipped agent or skill was configured at the moment of the report, read from its frontmatter: the effort it overrides the session to, and the model it pins, or null where it inherits.

with_transcript.description: How many of the invocations the usage and duration below actually sum over. Where it is below `invocations`, the totals are a floor, and the report says so.
